intro: My research focuses on Secure and dependable intelligent systems. The following interests connect learning foundations, system assurance and applications in cybersecurity.

areas.title: Trustworthy AI & Cybersecurity
areas.description:
My work examines how AI systems can support security decisions that are reliable, interpretable and useful in practice. Insider threat detection and behavioural analytics provide an application setting for studying how models respond to changing user activity and uncertain evidence.

This direction connects predictive performance with the quality of the decisions a model supports, including false alarms, generalisation and the interpretation of model outputs.
areas.notes:
How can security models remain useful when user behaviour changes?
How can confidence estimates and explanations support the review of alerts?

areas.title: Theoretical Analysis of Neural Networks
areas.description:
This research interest concerns the foundations and behaviour of neural learning systems. It involves examining the relationship between model structure, learned representations and the behaviour of a model when its inputs or operating conditions change.

The aim is to connect empirical observations with clear assumptions and analytical reasoning, supporting a better understanding of when neural models can be relied upon.
areas.notes:
Which properties of a model help explain its behaviour?
How can theoretical analysis inform the design and evaluation of learning systems?

areas.title: Machine Unlearning for Secure AI
areas.description:
Machine unlearning studies how the influence of selected training information can be removed from an already trained model. My interest is in understanding this process in the context of secure AI and dependable model behaviour.

Relevant questions include how to evaluate whether removal has been effective, how retained knowledge is affected, and how the resulting model compares with a model retrained without the selected information.
areas.notes:
How can the effect of unlearning be evaluated?
How can removal effectiveness be balanced with retained model utility?

areas.title: Formal Specification & Verification Systems
areas.description:
Formal specification provides a precise way to express the behaviour expected from a system. Verification examines whether that behaviour satisfies the stated requirements under explicit assumptions.

My interest is in how these ideas can support dependable computational and AI systems, particularly where clearly defined properties and careful reasoning about system behaviour are important.
areas.notes:
Which requirements can be expressed as verifiable properties?
How can verification complement empirical evaluation?

areas.title: Neuro-Symbolic Models
areas.description:
Neuro-symbolic models combine the ability of neural networks to learn from data with the explicit knowledge and reasoning provided by symbolic systems. This approach allows domain knowledge, logical rules and constraints to guide learning and support the interpretation of model decisions.

My research interest lies in exploring how these models can improve the reliability, interpretability and consistency of AI systems, particularly in cybersecurity and insider threat detection. Potential directions include incorporating security rules into behavioural learning models, identifying inconsistencies between predictions and domain knowledge, and developing explanations that connect observed behaviour with explicit reasoning.
areas.notes:
How can symbolic knowledge guide or constrain learned behaviour?
When do hybrid representations improve a learning task?
